items.title: Separation of a k-rational point from finitely many points by a section of a very ample invertible sheaf
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The statement produces a global section of a very ample invertible sheaf on a finite type k-scheme that vanishes at a prescribed k-rational point x and at none of finitely many other points x_1,...,x_n (statement lines 4232-4241). The proof first reduces a very ample L on X to the model case X = P^r_k with L = O_X(1) (proof lines 4244-4247), then identifies V = H^0(X, O_X(1)) with the linear forms and the sections vanishing at x with a codimension one subspace W that generates the homogeneous prime ideal of x (proof lines 4248-4253); the non-formal step is the final one, where each x_i != x gives a homogeneous prime p_i not containing W, so W is not the union of the finitely many W cap p_i because k is infinite (proof lines 4253-4256). The claim is H2: the reduction is standard and the last step is the finite-union-of-proper-subspaces argument over an infinite field.
